{{Quote|Five, you don’t want one. They melt. Don’t you remember? Kaird told us he’d seen one melt.|[[Den Dhur]]|<ref name="The Last Jedi">[[The Last Jedi (novel)|''The Last Jedi'']]</ref>}}
The '''BB-3000''' was a [[Human replica droid]] model that was produced by [[LeisureMech Enterprises/Legends|LeisureMech Enterprises]] during the early [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Their [[Droid/Legends|droid]] bodies were encased in [[Cloning/Legends|cloned]] [[Synthflesh/Legends|synthflesh]] to make them appear identical to a living being. The droid brain of the BB-3000 would somehow get contaminated with the synthflesh's cloned genome. This resulted in the development of a strange hybrid virus that was partly RNA from the cloned tissue, and partly hardwired memetic algorithm from the substratum operating system. The droid's hybrid virus would catch the droid between two modalities of being, overload its sensorium circuitry, and cause its internal temperature to rapidly fluctuate until it melted.<ref name="Street of Shadows">[[Coruscant Nights II: Street of Shadows|''Coruscant Nights I: Street of Shadows'']]</ref> LeisureMech abandoned trying to solve this issue and instead moved on to develop the [[BB-4000]].<ref name="The Last Jedi" />

By [[19 BBY/Legends|18.8 BBY]], [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]] of [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] had established a secret [[Abandoned droid factory|HRD laboratory]] in the abandoned [[Factory District]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant's]] [[Antipodes]] region. Xizor planned to subtly usurp control of Black Sun by replacing [[Underlord]] [[Dal Perhi]] with a BB-3000 [[Dal Perhi (droid)|HRD puppet]]. Xizor considered the BB-3000 HRDs to be the first real advancement in droid manufacturing technology in a dozen centuries. His plan was foiled when his HRD melted.<ref name="Street of Shadows" />
